Subject: High inference latency in checkout - urgent

Laura / Marissa —

We’ve just seen a significant degradation in inference performance affecting our checkout flow. Error rate jumped to ~5% and tail latency is spiking to 6–12s for text-generation endpoints. This started at ~07:55 PT and is impacting roughly 9% of requests from our EU customers. We’ve switched traffic to the fallback endpoint but that only partially mitigates the problem.

Attached: polestar_request_sysdump.txt (request traces, top-sampled logs).

This is causing failed payment authorizations — finance is flagging lost revenue. We need an ETA for remediation and a concrete mitigation plan. Please escalate.

— Alex

Joining 08:30 — I’m already pulling runtime traces. Initial observations:

- Bump in KV cache miss rate starting 07:52 PT for polestar-prod region-us-west-2.
- One of the dedicated Dedicated pools (dedicated-03) shows higher soft-GPU preemption count; suspected noisy neighbor on the host.
- Error spike correlates with requests hitting the v2-long-context variant.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: can you upload sampled request payloads & model choice breakdown to the Drive folder? I’ve attached a short sysdump.
- Marcus: suggest we temporarily re-route polestar-prod traffic to v1-short-context + reduce max_tokens to 256 while we investigate.

I’ll open a prioritized infra remediation ticket and request host remediation with cloud provider.

Attachments: polestar_request_sysdump.txt

— Jonas Weber
Sr. Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Agree with Jonas. Additional notes from an exec standpoint:

- I authorize temporary routing to v1-short-context for up to 48h while we stabilize — Laura, please prep SLA exception request and notify finance.
- Recommend enabling aggressive prefix caching and reducing concurrency per container to reduce tail latency; costs will increase modestly.
- If we see error-rate >3% after initial mitigation, we should plan a surge capacity uplift (Dedicated burst) and bring in cloud partner ops.

I’m looping Evelyn for customer comms tone and Marissa for telemetry to confirm the rollback steps.

Marcus Lin
